Nine US Companies Object to Tokenized Trading on OKXICE According to an OKXICE public notice dated October 15, the platform has received issuer objections from nine companies — Cerebras, AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave, Verizon, Applied Optoelectronics, Broadcom and UnitedHealth — meaning their shares will not be offered for tokenized trading on OKXICE TSV. OKXICE LLC is 50% owned by ICE, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, and 50% by OKC USA, and plans to offer 24/7 tokenized U.S. equity trading through a permissioned Uniswap v4 AMM on XLayer. — link

Highlight Clip: Justin Sun: Sold 80–90% of ETH at $3,600–$4,000, Then Bought Heavily Into US Stocks Justin Sun: Sold 80–90% of ETH at $3,600–$4,000, Then Bought Heavily Into US Stocks On October 16, 2026, Justin Sun said in an interview with William Joy that he had sold 80–90% of his ETH position at around $3,600–$4,000, keeping only a core holding and had not bought back in as of the interview. He said ETH appeared to have formed a fragile double top, prompting him to cut his position sharply, while leaving his core Bitcoin holdings untouched. He subsequently bought heavily into US stocks, expecting capital to concentrate in that market. — link

Anthropic Proposes $1B Loss or 50-Casualty Threshold for AI Intervention According to POLITICO, Anthropic has been pitching U.S. lawmakers on an unpublished draft bill for frontier AI safety. The proposal would allow the government to seek restrictions on a model’s release or use only if it poses a foreseeable and imminent risk of more than $1 billion in damages or at least 50 deaths or serious injuries, including risks involving biological weapons, loss of developer control or cyberattacks. The draft would also require regular independent evaluations of frontier models and place some state-level AI safety rules under a federal framework. — link
